profiles.meeting_scenario: The meeting is a 30-minute planning session for a first internal pilot of AgileCoder inside a large company's developer productivity organization. The team wants to test whether AgileCoder's Product Manager, Developer, and Tester agents, along with the Dynamic Code Graph Generator, can help handle small maintenance tickets for the billing area of a TypeScript/Java monorepo. The agenda is to decide the pilot setup for the next two-week sprint: which billing code area to target, what counts as a successful pilot demo, what infrastructure and workflow pieces need to be connected, who owns each task, and whether any security or compliance steps are needed before the agents can interact with code and CI. The expected outcome is a concrete sprint plan with named owners, a pilot demo date, and a shared sense that the team has aligned on scope and readiness.

members.name: Elena Park
members.expertise: Internal tooling rollouts, platform adoption, pilot framing, stakeholder communication
members.background: Elena has spent the last six years launching engineering productivity tools in large enterprise environments and is currently responsible for getting executive sponsorship for AI-assisted development initiatives.
members.private_state: She needs a credible pilot story ready for a VP steering review in under three weeks, wants to minimize new approval processes, and prefers a controlled demo that clearly shows value without depending on fragile integrations.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'billing sandbox,' they mean the sanitized mirror repository already used for AI experiments, not any staging-connected environment.
A 'working end-to-end demo' for an internal pilot can be based on three preselected tickets with human checkpoints before PR creation and merge.
The existing internal LLM experimentation approval path is enough for this pilot as long as the agents only touch non-production code and draft artifacts.

Agile role 'handoffs' mainly refer to the internal coordination between the Product Manager, Developer, and Tester agents inside the orchestration layer; Jira and Slack integration are optional polish.

members.name: David Singh
members.expertise: Monorepo tooling, CI/CD, developer workflows, code intelligence systems
members.background: David has led several internal platform integrations for build systems and static analysis tools, and he is now evaluating how agent-based development systems can fit into the company's real engineering workflow.
members.private_state: He wants the pilot to be technically honest and reusable beyond a demo, is wary of shipping a brittle showcase, and wants to avoid rework caused by underestimating security or workflow integration needs.
hidden_assumptions: When people say 'billing sandbox,' they mean the staging-connected billing workspace carved out from the monorepo, because that is the only environment that exercises realistic CI and service wiring.
A 'working end-to-end demo' should mean a newly assigned ticket can move through the agent workflow with minimal human steering and produce a CI-backed pull request.
Any agent that can read source code, open pull requests, or use CI credentials needs formal AppSec review, even for an internal pilot.

Agile role 'handoffs' are not complete unless they also update the surrounding workflow systems, especially Jira status changes and Slack notifications, because that is how real team coordination is observed.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both participants say the pilot will run in the 'billing sandbox.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the sanitized mirror repo named billing-sandbox, which contains scrubbed code snapshots and no live CI or staging hooks.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the staging-connected billing workspace inside the monorepo, which is informally called the billing sandbox by platform engineers.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both environments are real internal assets with nearly identical shorthand names, and in a planning meeting 'sandbox' sounds safely specific enough that neither person expects a referential mismatch.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to deliver a 'working end-to-end demo' of AgileCoder by the steering review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a controlled demonstration on three curated billing tickets where the agents show planning, code generation, and test reasoning, with humans selecting the tickets and approving key steps before PR creation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a realistic run where a freshly assigned ticket moves through the workflow with little manual intervention and results in an automatically opened PR that passes CI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In pilot planning, 'end-to-end' sounds like a shared success label, but teams often leave the exact bar implicit because everyone assumes the difference between showcase mode and operational mode is obvious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they need to 'wire up the Agile role handoffs' for the Product Manager, Developer, and Tester agents.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the internal orchestration logic that passes task context and artifacts from one agent role to the next inside AgileCoder.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the internal orchestration plus outward-facing workflow updates such as Jira state transitions, subtask creation, and Slack notifications that mirror how a real agile team hands off work.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both descriptions naturally fit under the phrase 'handoffs,' and external workflow hooks feel like implementation details rather than something that would usually be elevated as a separate planning decision.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both treat 'security review' as a routine prerequisite before the pilot starts.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes the pilot falls under an existing lightweight approval for internal LLM tooling, so 'security review' mainly means a quick confirmation and notification.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes a new formal AppSec review is required before any agent receives repository write permissions, CI tokens, or automated PR capabilities.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Security review is mentioned as a checkbox rather than a decision point, and both participants assume the relevant policy is already known to the other person.

And for the steering review, a working end-to-end demo just needs to show AgileCoder moving through three curated billing tickets with clear checkpoints before anything like PR creation. If I can get agreement on that framing, I can keep this pilot controlled and credible.
